name: Our World in Data
publisher: Global Change Data Lab / University of Oxford
description: Several thousand curated, harmonised long-run indicators on emissions, energy, health, poverty, food, war and democracy - assembled from primary statistical sources, documented, and served as tidy CSV straight off each chart's URL. The fastest route from a question to a defensible, citable time series.

license.name: CC-BY 4.0 for OWID's own work; upstream sources keep their terms
license.redistribution: permitted with attribution to OWID and the underlying source

access.size_hint: a single indicator CSV is typically under 5 MB
access.etiquette: append ?v=1&csvType=full to a grapher URL rather than scraping the chart

probes.description: Any chart's underlying data, as CSV, from the chart's own slug

recipes.title: Turn any OWID chart into a dataframe
recipes.code:
import pandas as pd
slug = 'annual-co2-emissions-per-country'   # the last path segment of any OWID chart URL
df = pd.read_csv('https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/%s.csv?v=1&csvType=full' % slug)
print(df.head())
# metadata for the same chart:
# https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/<slug>.metadata.json

gotchas.trap: The Entity column mixes countries, continents and income groups, so a naive sum double-counts.
gotchas.fix: Rows with a blank Code, or a Code like OWID_WRL, are aggregates. Filter them out.

gotchas.trap: OWID harmonises and sometimes rescales upstream data, so figures can differ slightly from the original agency's.
gotchas.fix: Cite both OWID and the underlying source; the .metadata.json names it.
